new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for cent2098; this is the first explicit statement and it covers exactly the two lects (Batu Belah, Long Teru) that Burkhardt, Burkhardt & Ang 2020 (JBK 6(1) p. 2 fn. 1) identify with ISO zbc / Central Berawan. Opened from an Internet Archive copy already held by the project, not from the listed open_url, which is currently blocked.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final (ultimate) syllable in both lects that make up Central Berawan (Batu Belah and Long Teru), as in all Berawan varieties; words are at most trisyllabic.
new_statements.identity_note: ISO zbc 'Central Berawan' = the Batu Belah (BB) and Long Teru (LTU) lects (Burkhardt, Burkhardt & Ang 2020, JBK 6(1) p. 2 fn. 1, held by the project in this folder). Only Burkhardt 2014 sections 5.2 and 5.3 describe these two lects directly. Clayre & Wan 1996 and Burkhardt 2006/2008 (indexes 1-3) describe the Long Terawan dialect on the Tutoh river = West Berawan (zbw; READALL lists it as west2564 'Berawan, Long Terawan dialect'); Clayre's analysis is based on a single speaker. Burkhardt 2014 (pp. 79, 193) states that all Berawan varieties share final syllable stress, so the Long Terawan statements are consistent with, but not evidence for, the Central Berawan reading.
